topic: What antenna design considerations optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations?
response: To optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations, antenna design should prioritize high gain and narrow beamwidth to maximize signal strength within the limited time frame. A high-gain antenna with a low side-lobe level can help maintain signal quality despite the satellite's rapid movement. The antenna's half-power beamwidth (HPBW) should be designed to match the satellite's visibility period, ensuring maximum signal reception during this brief window.
reference_context: The reference context discusses LEO constellations with satellites at an altitude of around 900 km and inclination of 74º, covering a service zone radius of more than 2500 km. The time of satellite flight over a subscriber can range from 10 minutes to 20 minutes.
